builder-academic.text:
Dr Jane Smith
Postdoctoral Researcher, Computational Neuroscience
j.smith@university.edu • +44 20 0000 0000 • Oxford, UK
janesmith.github.io • github.com/janesmith • ORCID 0000-0002-1825-0097

Profile
Computational modelling of neural circuits, Bayesian inference in sensory processing and machine
learning for neuroimaging.

Education
Ph.D. in Computational Neuroscience

Oct. 2019 – Sept. 2023

University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK
Thesis: Probabilistic models of predictive coding in visual cortex

M.Sc. in Mathematics

Sept. 2017 – June 2019

Imperial College London, London, UK

Experience
Postdoctoral Research Fellow

Oct. 2023 – present

University of Oxford, Oxford, UK
Built a Bayesian decoder that cut analysis time for 7T fMRI data by 40%
Leads a team of 3 PhD students and 2 master’s interns

Publications
Journal articles
1. Smith, J. & Researcher, A. (2023). Efficient coding with correlated neural noise. PLOS
Computational Biology.
Conference papers
1. Chen, L., Smith, J. & Okafor, N. (2024). Predictive coding as amortised inference. Advances in
Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS).
Preprints
1. Smith, J. (2025). Sparse priors for laminar fMRI. bioRxiv.

Grants and fellowships
• 2023 – 2025: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship (EUR 215,000)

Teaching and supervision
• 2024: Lecturer, Bayesian Models of Cognition (M.Sc., 40 students)
• 2020 – 2022: Supervisor, Part II Neuroscience, University of Cambridge

Invited talks
• 2024: Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, London

Awards
• 2023: Best Thesis Prize, Cambridge Neuroscience

Service
• Reviewer for PLOS Computational Biology and NeurIPS

References
Prof. Alan Turner, University of Cambridge, a.turner@cam.ac.uk

Skills
Programming
Tools
Languages

Python, PyTorch, JAX, R
Git, LaTeX, Slurm, Docker
English (native), French (B2)
